fluorite.options.rt.title: Fluorite Ray Tracing
fluorite.options.rt.category.tracing.too: Samples, bounces, the sun's angular size, and whether entities and particles are traced.
fluorite.options.rt.category.postProcess: Exposure, output transform, colour grading, and lens effects.
fluorite.options.rt.category.material.to: Surface response: the sun's estimators, anisotropic highlights and subsurface scattering.
fluorite.options.rt.category.water.toolt: Waves on the surface, and how much the water itself scatters light.
fluorite.options.rt.category.fog.tooltip: The world's air: density, height profile, distance limits, and how it scatters the sun.
fluorite.options.rt.category.weather.too: Global wind and continuous time, rain and thunder responses for fog, clouds and water.
Overrides that affect one dimension without changing the Overworld or other presets.
fluorite.options.rt.category.upscaling.t: DLSS Ray Reconstruction. Off traces at display resolution and shows the raw path trace.
fluorite.options.rt.category.diagnostics: Render a guide buffer instead of the world.
fluorite.options.rt.exposureMode.tooltip: How the ray-traced image is mapped to display brightness. Auto adapts to scene luminance; Manual uses the exposure value directly.
fluorite.options.rt.manualEv.tooltip: Exposure compensation in stops. In Manual, this is the fixed exposure. In Auto, this biases the auto exposure brighter or darker.
fluorite.options.rt.autoExposureCompensa: An EV offset applied only in Auto mode. Positive values make the histogram target brighter; this is not an absolute exposure.
fluorite.options.rt.manualExposureEv.too: The absolute exposure EV used only in Manual mode. It does not bias Auto mode.
fluorite.options.rt.brightAdaptationTime: Auto mode time constant when entering a brighter environment and lowering exposure. One time constant completes about 63% of the EV change; three complete about 95%.
fluorite.options.rt.darkAdaptationTime.t: Auto mode time constant when entering darkness and raising exposure. It is deliberately slower to approximate human dark adaptation.
fluorite.options.rt.outputTransform.tool: AgX is the fast compatibility default. ACES 2 LUT samples a pre-baked 65-cube for normal play; ACES 2 Exact evaluates the full fixed-version transform for reference.
fluorite.options.rt.acesHdrPreset.toolti: Official fixed ACES 2 Rec.2020/PQ output preset. Used only when both ACES 2 and HDR output are active.
fluorite.options.rt.colorGrading.tooltip: Enable scene-referred white balance and creative colour controls. Off is an exact bypass.
fluorite.options.rt.colorTemperature.too: Adapts D65 toward the selected colour temperature. 6500 K is neutral; lower is warmer and higher is cooler.
fluorite.options.rt.colorTint.tooltip: Moves the adapted white point between green and magenta without changing exposure.
fluorite.options.rt.colorContrast.toolti: Scene-referred log contrast around 18% grey. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.colorSaturation.tool: Creative colour intensity after log contrast. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.colorHue.tooltip: Rotates hue in a luminance-preserving opponent space. 0 degrees is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.artisticGrading.tool: Open scene-linear global, shadow, midtone and highlight grading controls.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowExposure.toolt: Exposure applied smoothly inside the shadow range. 0 EV is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowRed.tooltip: Red-channel balance in the shadow range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowGreen.tooltip: Green-channel balance in the shadow range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowBlue.tooltip: Blue-channel balance in the shadow range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowSaturation.too: Colour intensity inside the shadow range. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowContrast.toolt: Log-luminance contrast around the shadow boundary. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.midExposure.tooltip: Exposure applied smoothly inside the midtone range. 0 EV is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.midRed.tooltip: Red-channel balance in the midtone range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.midGreen.tooltip: Green-channel balance in the midtone range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.midBlue.tooltip: Blue-channel balance in the midtone range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.midSaturation.toolti: Colour intensity inside the midtone range. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.midContrast.tooltip: Log-luminance contrast around 18% grey. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightExposure.to: Exposure applied smoothly inside the highlight range. 0 EV is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightRed.tooltip: Red-channel balance in the highlight range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightGreen.toolt: Green-channel balance in the highlight range, measured in exposure stops.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightBlue.toolti: Blue-channel balance in the highlight range, measured in exposure stops.
Colour intensity inside the highlight range. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightContrast.to: Log-luminance contrast around the highlight boundary. 1.00x is neutral.
fluorite.options.rt.shadowBoundary.toolt: Centre of the smooth shadow-to-midtone transition, in stops relative to 18% grey.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightBoundary.to: Centre of the smooth midtone-to-highlight transition, in stops relative to 18% grey.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrain.tooltip: Add dynamic monochrome grain after grading and before the SDR or HDR output transform. UI is unaffected.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrainIntensity.t: Overall zero-centred scene-linear grain strength. 0 is an exact bypass.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrainSize.toolti: Approximate display-pixel size of each grain sample.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrainChromatic.t: Mix independently shifted R, G and B noise into the shared luminance grain. 0 is monochrome film-like grain; 1 approaches coloured analogue-TV noise.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrainShadows.too: Multiplier for grain inside the artistic grading shadow range.
fluorite.options.rt.filmGrainMidtones.to: Multiplier for grain inside the artistic grading midtone range.
Multiplier for grain inside the artistic grading highlight range.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightThreshold.t: Shared Bloom/Lens Flare threshold after exposure but before the output transform. 1 is reference display white; lower values admit more of the image.
fluorite.options.rt.highlightSoftKnee.to: Width of the smooth transition around the shared highlight threshold. 0 is hard; 1 begins the transition one threshold below it.
fluorite.options.rt.bloom.tooltip: Diffuse visible HDR highlights into a local scene-linear glow. It is independently switchable from Lens Flare and does not affect exposure metering or UI.
fluorite.options.rt.bloomIntensity.toolt: Amount of the reconstructed multi-resolution glow added back to the scene.
fluorite.options.rt.bloomRadius.tooltip: How strongly coarse pyramid levels spread highlights across the image. It changes width without silently changing the shared threshold.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlare.tooltip: Add an artistic camera-lens approximation driven only by visible HDR highlights: ghosts, a halo and anamorphic streaks. It is not physical lens ray tracing.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareIntensity.t: Master strength for all Lens Flare components.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareGhosts.tool: Strength of reflected, mildly tinted highlight copies mirrored through the image centre.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareHalo.toolti: Strength of the broad circular lens halo around the image centre.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareStreaks.too: Strength of horizontal anamorphic streaks emitted by visible highlights.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareThreshold.t: Independent display-relative brightness threshold for Lens Flare. Higher values prevent bright scenery from entering the ghost image; it no longer changes Bloom.
fluorite.options.rt.lensFlareBokehSize.t: Display-pixel radius of the procedural five-blade aperture convolution. Larger pentagons cost more because the quarter-resolution gather grows with radius squared.
fluorite.options.rt.lensEffects.tooltip: Open the classified film grain, Bloom, Lens Flare, focus, motion, lens geometry and framing controls.
fluorite.options.rt.lensEffects.title: Lens Effects
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfField.tooltip: Enable physically parameterised screen-space thin-lens blur. It runs after exposure metering, so the blur does not change automatic exposure.
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfFieldFocusMod: Auto tracks and smoothly follows the surface under the screen centre. Manual uses the Focus Distance slider.
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfFieldFocusDis: Manual optical focus distance in blocks. It is retained while auto focus is active.
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfFieldFStop.to: Lens f-number. Lower values make a wider aperture and shallower depth of field; f/32 is nearly pinhole-like.
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfFieldMaxRadiu: Safety clamp on the circle-of-confusion radius. Higher values allow stronger blur and wider bokeh but sample farther across the image.
fluorite.options.rt.depthOfFieldAperture: Circular is the neutral default. Five to nine blades shape out-of-focus highlights into a procedural diaphragm polygon.
fluorite.options.rt.motionBlur.tooltip: Blur scene-linear radiance along the existing camera and object motion vectors, with depth rejection at silhouettes.
fluorite.options.rt.motionBlurShutterAng: Exposure duration relative to one rendered frame. 180 degrees exposes for half a frame; 0 removes blur.
fluorite.options.rt.motionBlurSamples.to: Samples along each motion vector. 16 is smoother and about twice the sampling work of 8.
Clamp on motion length in display pixels, preventing teleports and frame stalls from smearing across the screen.
fluorite.options.rt.lensDistortion.toolt: Enable aspect-correct radial lens distortion in scene-linear HDR. Barrel distortion is automatically cropped to avoid black borders; UI and exposure metering are unaffected.
fluorite.options.rt.lensDistortionStreng: Signed linked radial curve: negative values produce barrel distortion and positive values produce pincushion distortion. 0 is an exact bypass.
Enable an artistic lateral RGB lens offset before exposure and the output transform. UI is not affected.
fluorite.options.rt.chromaticAberrationS: Maximum red/blue radial separation at the image edge in display pixels. 0 is an exact bypass.
fluorite.options.rt.vignette.tooltip: Enable a smooth elliptical corner darkening before the output transform. Exposure metering and UI are not affected.
fluorite.options.rt.vignetteIntensity.to: How dark the outer vignette becomes. 0 is an exact bypass; 1 can reach black at the corners.
fluorite.options.rt.vignetteStart.toolti: Normalised radius where darkening begins. Lower values move the effect farther toward the centre.
fluorite.options.rt.vignetteSoftness.too: Width of the transition from the clear centre to the darkened border.
fluorite.options.rt.spp.tooltip: Path-tracing samples taken per pixel each frame. Higher is cleaner but more demanding.
fluorite.options.rt.maxBounces.tooltip: Maximum number of secondary path-tracing bounces after the primary hit. Higher captures more indirect light but costs more.
fluorite.options.rt.restirReuseDepth.too: How many path bounces keep a reservoir between frames. 0 disables ReSTIR reuse. Measured: the first depth accepts 93-97% of its stored reservoirs. Deeper ones accept under 1% on their own, but about 15% (depth 2) and 9% (depth 3) once ReSTIR Spatial Neighbours is on, because a neighbour is judged by whether it is the same surface rather than the same point. Whether that is worth the memory is not measured. Each depth costs about 530 MB at 1920x1080 and 1 sample per pixel.
fluorite.options.rt.restirSpatialNeighbo: How many nearby pixels each vertex borrows a light reservoir from. 0 is off. Costs no video memory at all - a neighbour is read from storage the reuse-depth dial already paid for - but each one costs arithmetic. Neighbours come from the previous frame, so a borrowed sample is a frame old. Does nothing unless ReSTIR Reuse Depth is above 0.
fluorite.options.rt.dynamicRisCandidates: How many light samples per surface go to entities, held blocks and flame particles instead of the world's own lights. 0 is off, and off is today's picture - those emitters have been collected since M18 and sampled by nothing, so a mob holding a torch lights itself and nothing around it. Their share of the budget is fixed rather than weighted by brightness, so a single mob and a room full of torches get the same number of samples.
fluorite.options.rt.emitterBrightness.to: One brightness over every finite emitter: block lights, entity and held-item lights, and the glow of the emissive surface itself - so a torch in a hand and the same torch in a wall stay equally bright. Does not touch the sun, the moon or the sky. 1.0x is off and is the shipped picture exactly.
fluorite.options.rt.emitterTemperature.t: Colour temperature for those same emitters, in kelvin. Off keeps each emitter's own colour. A real blackbody temperature, normalised so it changes what colour the lights are and never how bright they are - a torch is near 1800K, a lantern near 2000K, daylight near 6500K. It applies to emitters that are not incandescent at all, like glowstone, which is an art choice rather than physics.
fluorite.options.rt.restirStats.tooltip: Writes the per-depth ReSTIR temporal-reuse acceptance rate to latest.log once a second. This is how you find out whether a reuse depth is earning its 265 MB or storing data that is rejected every frame. Diagnostic only, and does nothing while ReSTIR Reuse Depth is 0.
fluorite.options.rt.sunSize.tooltip: Angular radius of the sun and moon disk. Larger discs cast softer shadow penumbrae.
fluorite.options.rt.entities.tooltip: Include entities and block entities in the ray-traced scene.
fluorite.options.rt.particles.tooltip: Draw particles as camera-ray billboards inside the traced scene.
fluorite.options.rt.particleShadows.tool: Let particles cast shadows, so a column of campfire smoke darkens the ground beneath it. Shadow rays only: particles stay out of reflections and GI, where a camera-facing billboard would be seen edge-on. Costs any-hit work on every shadow ray that crosses a particle.
fluorite.options.rt.glow.tooltip: Draw the vanilla Glowing-effect outline (through walls) around glowing entities.
fluorite.options.rt.waterWaves.tooltip: Animate water-surface normals for moving wave highlights.
fluorite.options.rt.waterCausticDispersi: Colour fringing in the caustic pattern. 1.0x is water's real dispersion — the three primaries refract slightly differently, which shows up along the bright filaments because that is where the focusing is sharpest. 0 is monochrome; above 1.0x exaggerates it.
fluorite.options.rt.waterScatterSource.t: Which light feeds the water's scattering. A diagnostic: the sun and the sky are occluded by different mechanisms, so isolating one is how you find out which is misbehaving. None keeps the water's opacity and removes only the added light.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSunShadow.toolt: Use the transmittance measured by water's fixed three stratified rays. Off still traces those rays for water depth but treats the sun as unoccluded — a diagnostic independent of the air-fog visibility setting.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSim.tooltip: Solve the water surface on a grid so ripples spread, reflect off blocks and interfere. Off leaves the procedural wave spectrum exactly as it was.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimRange.toolti: How far the simulated water reaches. The grid is a fixed 256 cells, so this is the cell size in disguise: 64 blocks gives ripples down to about half a block, 128 gives twice the reach for half the detail. Reach and detail are two ends of one stick.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimHeight.toolt: How far above or below you the simulation will look for a water surface. The other half of which water ripples: the range says how wide the domain is, this says how tall a slice of the world it may sit in. Symmetric about you, so it holds whether you are under the surface looking up or flying above it.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimReanchor.too: How far you may walk before the domain follows. Re-anchoring is the only thing here that costs more than one dispatch -- it recasts the obstacle mask -- and between re-anchors the domain is completely still. Ripples are damped long before they reach the edge, so there is little to gain from a small value.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimStrength.too: How much of the simulated slope reaches the shading, against the procedural spectrum's. The two are added, so this is the ripples' share rather than a replacement.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimSpeed.toolti: How fast a ripple travels, in blocks per second. Clamped against the solver's stability limit, which depends on the timestep and the cell size -- past it the scheme does not lose accuracy, it amplifies every step.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimDamping.tool: How much of a ripple survives each step. Lower makes water settle sooner. An approximation: real water loses energy fastest at the shortest wavelengths and this is a uniform loss.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimImpulse.tool: How much surface an entity moving through the water may displace. A stability guard as much as a look: a displacement large enough against the cell size steepens the slope until the next step overshoots, and the overshoot compounds.
fluorite.options.rt.waveLength.tooltip: The longest wave in the sea; nine shorter ones follow from it, each about a third shorter than the last. There is deliberately no speed setting: deep-water physics ties speed to wavelength, so shortening the swell slows it down on its own and the relative speeds across the spectrum stay real. Amplitude follows too, because what is authored is steepness -- so this is the difference between a choppy pond and an ocean swell, not just a scale.
fluorite.options.rt.waveAmplitude.toolti: How tall the waves are. 1 is the original look, exactly. It scales the shape and the tilt together, because they are the same surface -- so raising it does not only make the water deform more, it also makes the reflections choppier and more broken. The original value was chosen when only the normal used it, and leaves the surface about 2.5 cm tall; real water under a light breeze is several times steeper, around 3 to 8 here.
How big a patch something disturbs, as a multiple of its own width. This is the ripple's WAVELENGTH: the solver treats every wavelength as travelling at the same speed, so a ripple's size is not a property of the water at all -- it is set entirely by whatever disturbed it. Turn it up past two or three blocks and the ripples grow long enough to move the water's actual geometry instead of only its reflections.
fluorite.options.rt.waterSimImpulseDepth: How deep something can be and still disturb the surface, measured from its highest point. A surface wave's motion decays exponentially with depth, so a swimmer well under it is not coupled to the surface at all. Faded across the range rather than cut off at the end of it, so swimming down does not pop.
fluorite.options.rt.waterDeform.tooltip: Move the water's actual geometry with the waves, instead of only tilting its normal. This is what a normal cannot fake: a wavy silhouette against the sky, crests casting shadows into the troughs, and a shoreline the waves ride up and down. Off is the original flat surface, exactly as it was, and costs nothing.
fluorite.options.rt.waterDeformRange.too: How far from you the water is real geometry. Beyond it the surface is flat and the waves live in the normal, as they always have. THE COST IS QUADRATIC IN THIS -- doubling the range quadruples the triangles, and every one of them is rebuilt each frame. The displacement is centimetres, so it reads as shape only up close.
fluorite.options.rt.waterDeformCell.tool: Blocks per mesh cell in the deformed region -- the other half of the triangle count. It is also the limit on what shape the geometry can hold: waves shorter than about two cells stay in the normal. Coarse cells lose less than you would think, because the long components carry almost all of the height.
How far you may walk before the deformed region follows you. Its own control rather than the ripples', because the two cost different things: that one recasts an obstacle mask, this one rebuilds a vertex grid.
fluorite.options.rt.waterPhaseG.tooltip: Forward bias of the water's scattering. Positive puts a halo around the sun seen from below. Strongly scattering water is driven toward isotropic on its own, since light that reaches the eye from deep down has been redirected many times.
fluorite.options.rt.waterScatterStrength: Arithmetic-mean scattering coefficient per block. This alone controls magnitude; the RGB controls below only set the relative colour shape.
fluorite.options.rt.waterScatterR.toolti: Red component of the scattering colour shape. Changing colour does not change the arithmetic-mean scattering strength.
fluorite.options.rt.waterScatterG.toolti: Green component of the scattering colour shape. Changing colour does not change the arithmetic-mean scattering strength.
fluorite.options.rt.waterScatterB.toolti: Blue component of the scattering colour shape. Changing colour does not change the arithmetic-mean scattering strength.
Take absorption from the sliders below instead of from the biome's water colour. Turns off per-biome variation.
Arithmetic-mean absorption coefficient per block for Manual Absorption. This alone controls magnitude; the RGB controls below only set the relative colour shape.
fluorite.options.rt.waterAbsorbR.tooltip: Red component of the absorption shape. High red removes red fastest and reads as cyan water; changing colour does not change mean strength.
fluorite.options.rt.waterAbsorbG.tooltip: Green component of the absorption shape. High green removes green fastest and reads as magenta water; changing colour does not change mean strength.
fluorite.options.rt.waterAbsorbB.tooltip: Blue component of the absorption shape. High blue removes blue fastest and reads as yellow water; changing colour does not change mean strength.
fluorite.options.rt.hdr.tooltip: SDR writes Rec.709 primaries with sRGB encoding. HDR10 writes a Rec.2020 container with ST.2084/PQ when supported; changing this requires a restart and falls back to SDR if unavailable.
fluorite.options.rt.hdrPaperWhite.toolti: Legacy AgX HDR only: absolute brightness that SDR-equivalent scene brightness maps to. ACES 2 uses its fixed preset instead.
fluorite.options.rt.hdrPeak.tooltip: Legacy AgX HDR only: absolute brightness highlights roll off toward. ACES 2 uses its fixed preset instead.
fluorite.options.rt.dlssQuality.tooltip: DLSS Ray Reconstruction quality mode. Lower-quality modes render fewer pixels and upscale more aggressively for higher framerates; higher-quality modes render more pixels for a sharper image. Only affects the image when DLSS Ray Reconstruction is enabled.
fluorite.options.rt.debugView.tooltip: Visualize an intermediate ray-tracing buffer instead of the final image.
fluorite.options.rt.debugView.18.tooltip: The accumulated fraction of the upper hemisphere reaching this pixel camera-segment midpoint. Blue sealed, green a little, yellow about half, orange most, red fully open; dimmed while the cell is still gathering samples.
fluorite.options.rt.fog.tooltip: The world's ambient participating medium. Integrated per path segment, so it appears in reflections and refractions, not just the direct view.
fluorite.options.rt.fogDensity.tooltip: Multiplier over the dimension's authored density. 1.0 is as authored.
fluorite.options.rt.netherFogEnabled.too: Enable the Nether preset's fog only. The global Volumetric Fog switch remains the master control. Off keeps local surface lighting and the low readability floor, but removes Nether fog extinction, scattering and its emitter shadow rays.
fluorite.options.rt.netherFogDensity.too: Additional 0–2 multiplier over the Nether preset. 1.0 keeps the authored density; after the global and Nether controls combine, the final player gain is still capped at 2. The limit avoids distant green reconstruction artifacts observed with dense fog under DLSS Ray Reconstruction.
fluorite.options.rt.netherAmbientBrightn: Multiplier over the Nether preset's neutral environment Radiance. It keeps the surface readability floor, escaped background and fog or water environment source consistent; it does not boost lava, glowstone or other local emitters. 1.0 is as authored.
fluorite.options.rt.endEnvironmentBright: Independent 0–8× multiplier over the End's full-sphere HDR star environment and its ambient contribution. It does not change the Kerr accretion disk. 1.0 is the authored value.
fluorite.options.rt.endEnvironmentRotati: Rotate only the escaped HDR environment around the Kerr spin axis, using continuous game time. The hole and disk stay fixed. Range 0–1 degrees per second; default 0.02.
fluorite.options.rt.endDiskBrightness.to: Independent 0–8× multiplier over visible Kerr accretion-disk emission and the matching direct-light estimate. It does not change the starfield. 1.0 is the authored value.
fluorite.options.rt.endDiskOuterRadius.t: Runtime outer edge in gravitational radii M. The Kerr path data retains the complete 12 M domain, so 4–12 M changes the actual disk support without rebuilding assets. Default 8 M.
fluorite.options.rt.endDiskThickness.too: Multiplier over the independently authored 0.55 M half-height. It changes the volume's silhouette, density and transmittance rather than merely dimming a static image. Range 0.25–2×; default 1×.
fluorite.options.rt.fogAlbedo.tooltip: Multiplier over the preset's single-scattering albedo. The 0–1 range keeps scattering no greater than extinction; 1.0 is as authored.
fluorite.options.rt.fogStart.tooltip: Distance in front of the camera that stays clear. Keeps the near field readable instead of veiling the whole screen.
fluorite.options.rt.fogCull.tooltip: Distance past which a segment stops accumulating fog, so distant terrain stays readable.
fluorite.options.rt.fogHeightScale.toolt: How far above the layer height the density has to climb before it drops to about a third. Small values give a shallow ground-hugging layer, large ones a deep haze.
fluorite.options.rt.fogPhaseG.tooltip: Henyey-Greenstein anisotropy. Positive values concentrate a glow around the sun; 0 scatters evenly in all directions.
fluorite.options.rt.fogTint.tooltip: Named scattering hue. The dimension preset supplies the exact colour; this shifts it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogSunShadowRays.too: Jittered shadow rays the ambient air fog sun term gets per marched segment. Never water. The cached grid used to sit at 0 and was removed: it was both slower (it made the bake cast 131k sun rays a frame) and blurrier (trilinear filtering cannot hold a shaft edge at any cell size).
fluorite.options.rt.volumeMultiScatter.t: Light reaching a scattering point decays at the diffusion rate rather than the beam's. Fixes dense fog and deep water going black: scattering removes light from the beam, not from the medium. Off reproduces the old behaviour exactly.
Sample one scattering event per segment instead of assuming light is constant along it. Lets the water's sky term ask how open the sky is where the light actually scatters, instead of probing once at the segment's start and gating the whole segment by it. Noisier per frame: a single sampled event carries the exact weight where the stratified estimator it replaces keeps closed-form weights. Off is the shipped behaviour.
fluorite.options.rt.volumeEmitterNee.too: Let lava, torches and campfires light the fog and the water, not only the surfaces around them. Requires Volumetric Scatter Vertex, which supplies the point the emitter is sampled from. One emitter and one shadow ray per scattering segment, reusing the same light grid the surfaces use.
fluorite.options.rt.clouds.tooltip: A marched cloud deck on a spherical shell, so it curves away at the horizon and appears in reflections as well as overhead. First slice: the shape is there but the lighting is ambient only, so the clouds are lit and flat until the sun term and multiple scattering land.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudWindSpeed.toolt: How fast the whole cloud field drifts, in blocks per second. 0 freezes the sky. Costs nothing: the drift is subtracted from the field's origin before the shader ever samples it, so a cloud and its reflection cannot disagree about where it has drifted to.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudFieldScale.tool: How far apart the sky's clumps and clearings are — the 2D distribution, not the size of one cloud. Large values give a few broad banks with wide gaps; small values give a busy, evenly speckled sky. Cloud Size under Shape is the separate question of how big a single cloud within a clump is.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudWeather.tooltip: Let rain and thunder move the sky. Rain fills the sky in and thickens it; thunder builds the clouds upward into cumulonimbus. Both are added to what the sliders below say, so turn this off before authoring a sky with them.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCoverage.toolti: Shifts the whole coverage field: negative clears the sky, positive overcasts it. 0 is the broken sky the noise bakes.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudDensity.tooltip: Multiplies cloud density, and with it how opaque a cloud is. 1.0 is the authored sky.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudType.tooltip: Which family of cloud the sky is made of: negative flattens it toward stratus sheets, 0 is fair-weather cumulus, positive builds it toward cumulonimbus towers with anvil tops. Tall types are also denser, because a thunderhead is a cumulus light cannot get through.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudExtinction.tool: How much light a block of full-density cloud removes. Small because the deck is hundreds of blocks deep; what matters is the product.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudAltitude.toolti: Where the deck's floor sits. Every cloud's flat base lands here whatever its type, the way a real condensation altitude works. Vanilla's own clouds sit at 192.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudThickness.toolt: How deep the deck is. A cumulonimbus fills it; a stratus sheet occupies only its lowest tenth. Deep costs march steps only where a tall cloud actually stands.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudDetailScale.too: How big the bites taken out of a cloud's edges are. Smaller is wispier.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudSunSteps.toolti: Steps in the march that asks how much cloud stands between a point and the sun. This is what gives a cloud a lit side and a shaded side; 0 takes the sun as unoccluded and flattens every cloud. These run per in-cloud sample of the main march, so they multiply its cost rather than adding to it -- this is the dial to measure clouds with. The steps double in length, so the reach stays one deck deep whatever this is and only the near field's resolution moves.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudMultiScatter.to: Keep the inside of a thick cloud bright. Light that scatters has been removed from the sun's beam but not from the cloud, so it keeps travelling -- at an optical depth of twenty the direct beam is zero while this is still a third. Without it a cumulonimbus is a black silhouette with a lit edge. Off is single scattering exactly, not an approximation of it.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudPhaseG.tooltip: How strongly cloud droplets scatter light forward. The default is close to the measured value for water droplets, which are large against visible wavelengths and so scatter forward very strongly. High values make a cloud standing in front of the sun dark with a fierce glowing rim; low values make it evenly bright and flat.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudAlbedo.tooltip: How much of an interaction inside a cloud scatters rather than absorbs. Sets how deep light reaches: the multiple-scattering term decays at the square root of three times one minus this, so at the default light reaches about eighteen times deeper than the direct beam. Water droplets barely absorb, so the default sits near one -- lowering it is the honest way to make clouds darker, where raising extinction only makes them more opaque.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusPatchDiam: Mean world-space diameter of one rounded high-cloud patch. The fixed world-grid hash varies its exact scale, rotation, offset and one of ten CC0 shapes.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusPatchSpac: Spacing of the deterministic world grid that scatters rounded high-cloud patches. Larger values make broader clear gaps; the grid itself is never drawn.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusDensity.t: Shared optical-depth multiplier for both analytic high-cloud sheets, independently of the convective deck below.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusPatchStre: Independent optical-depth multiplier for the lower sheet of scattered rounded cloud patches. 0 removes only that sheet.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusWindSpeed: How fast both high-cloud shape fields drift, in blocks per second. Their wind is independent from the convective deck below.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudShadows.tooltip: Let clouds shade the ground, water and everything else the sun lights. Read from a transmittance map baked once a frame along the sun's direction, out of the same density field the clouds overhead are drawn from -- so a shadow cannot end up somewhere its cloud is not. One texture read per sun sample. Off also restores the old global weather fade on underwater caustics, which existed to stand in for this.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrus.tooltip: Two analytic high-cloud sheets above the main deck: deterministic rounded CC0 patches below and a seamless wispy field above. Both store optical depth only and are relit by the current sun and sky; neither runs the old high-cloud volume march.
Adds or removes optical depth from both high-cloud shape fields before Beer transmittance. It is independent of the convective deck below.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusExtinctio: Extinction per reference block used to convert both sheets' shape into optical depth. 0 turns both high-cloud sheets off.
Where the lower analytic high-cloud sheet sits. It is raised automatically to remain above the convective deck.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusThickness: Vertical separation and optical reference thickness of the two analytic high-cloud sheets: rounded patches sit at the bottom and the wispy field at the top.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudSecondary.toolt: Clouds visible to reflections, refractions and later bounces. Off removes them on secondary rays; Reduced lowers only the low-volume march and shadow budget, while the analytic high-cloud sheets keep the same world field. This never moves clouds relative to the direct sky.
fluorite.options.rt.waterMediumTrace.too: Writes low-rate centre-ray water radiance, segment length, visibility and terrain-streaming telemetry to latest.log. Diagnostic only; adds one upward ray per frame while enabled.
fluorite.options.rt.fogSegmentSource.too: Diagnostic: which segments of a path may add fog in-scatter. The froxel covers the camera segment; every bounce runs the unshadowed closed form.
fluorite.options.rt.fogInScatterSegments: How many bounces may add fog light, counted from the camera. 0 is every bounce, which is what ships. Lower values save shadow rays and marching in the deepest bounces, whose contribution is already small; the fog still HIDES distant geometry at every depth, so nothing goes missing in reflections.
fluorite.options.rt.fogScatterTintR.tool: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogScatterTintG.tool: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogScatterTintB.tool: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogExtinctionTintR.t: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogExtinctionTintG.t: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogExtinctionTintB.t: Luminance-preserving: moving these changes the fog colour and never its density. Colour tints the light the fog sends back to the eye; Absorption tints which wavelengths it removes from what is behind it.
fluorite.options.rt.fogHeightBase.toolti: World height the fog layer sits at. Density holds steady at and below this and thins out above it, so this moves the layer rather than reshaping it.
fluorite.options.rt.dlssEnabled.tooltip: Off traces at full resolution with no denoising and no temporal accumulation — the reference view for judging a material change on its own terms. Raise samples per pixel alongside it.
fluorite.options.rt.sunMis.tooltip: Weights the two ways the sun is estimated — a shadow ray toward it, and a reflection landing on it — instead of adding both. Only materials smoother than roughness 0.006 change; mirrors are untouched. Off to compare.
fluorite.options.rt.emitterMis.tooltip: Weights the two ways a torch, lantern or lava block is estimated — the light sampler aiming at it, and a bounce that lands on it — instead of taking both in full. Off also restores the highlight softening that hid the difference, so the pair moves together. Off to compare.
fluorite.options.rt.anisotropy.tooltip: Stretches the highlight along the surface grain, the way brushed metal and satin look. Only affects materials whose pack authored anisotropy.amount; everything else is identical either way. Off to compare.
fluorite.options.rt.subsurfaceMode.toolt: How light that enters a material is traced back out. Thin is a surface approximation with no interior — cheap, and right for a backlit leaf. Random walk actually walks the photon through the medium, which is what gives a thick material depth. Costs one traversal per scattering event; bound it with the budget below.
How thick the thin-shell mode treats a leaf or petal as being. 1.00 is the shipping look. Thicker transmits less light and scatters it more evenly; thinner is brighter and keeps more of the sun's direction, like a petal held up to it. One control because thickness drives both.
Scattering events one random walk may take. Cost is near-linear in this. Lowering it does not darken anything — a walk that runs out falls back to a diffuse bounce — it makes thick material less accurate. This is the lever to turn if subsurface is too expensive.
fluorite.options.rt.category.sky.tooltip: Sun and sky art direction on top of the physics.
fluorite.options.rt.sunIntensity.tooltip: Multiplies the sunlight and moonlight. 1.00x is the physical value.
fluorite.options.rt.sunTemperature.toolt: Colour temperature of the sunlight. Physical leaves the atmosphere's own colour alone.
fluorite.options.rt.skyIntensity.tooltip: Multiplies the sky's brightness. 1.00x is the physical value.
fluorite.options.rt.skyTemperature.toolt: Colour temperature of the sky. Physical leaves the atmosphere's own colour alone.
fluorite.options.rt.resetDefaults.toolti: Puts every Fluorite setting back to its shipped value.
fluorite.options.rt.windAngle.tooltip: The direction weather travels for the whole world. Fog, both cloud layers and the sea add their own signed offset and keep their own speed; only the heading is shared.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudWindOffset.tool: How far the cumulus deck runs off the global wind direction. Zero means it travels straight downwind.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudCirrusWindOffse: How far the cirrus sheet runs off the global wind direction. High ice really does travel at an angle to the surface wind, which is why this is an offset rather than something to zero out.
fluorite.options.rt.waveWindOffset.toolt: How far the swell runs off the global wind direction. The individual wave trains still fan out around it -- tightly for the long swell, widely for the short chop.
fluorite.options.rt.waveComplexity.toolt: How irregular the sea is. Ramps in a second wave system crossing the first, widens the fan of wave directions, and lets more of the wavefronts wander instead of ruling straight lines. The crossing system is the important part -- two wave trains interfere into a shifting lattice that reads as far more complex than one fan, and real water almost always has one, because a swell outlives the wind that made it. It does NOT add more waves: there are still ten. Zero is the original look.
fluorite.options.rt.waveCrossAngle.toolt: How far the second wave system runs off the first. Only has an effect while Wave Complexity is above zero.
fluorite.options.rt.waveGust.tooltip: How strongly gusts ruffle the surface. Without this the sea is equally rough everywhere, which is the single thing that most makes it read as a pattern instead of as weather -- real water is patchy, a dark ruffled stretch here and a glassy calm one there, with the boundary crawling downwind. Weighted toward the SHORT waves, because a gust ruffles a surface, it does not raise a swell. Costs three noise fetches per shaded point rather than per wave. Zero is the original look.
fluorite.options.rt.waveGustScale.toolti: How big one gust patch is. Small values give a busy stippled surface; large ones give slow broad sweeps of rough and calm.
fluorite.options.rt.waveGustSpeed.toolti: How fast the patches travel downwind. Zero pins them to the world, which looks like a stain on the sea -- the waves move through the patches while the patches sit still.
fluorite.options.rt.waveWeather.tooltip: How much rain and thunder move the sea. The clouds have always responded to the weather; the water did not, so a storm could roll in overhead while the sea below stayed as glassy as it was at noon. It drives three things, not one: the waves grow taller, steeper, and gustier -- and steepness is the part that actually reads as violent, because scaling only the height gives a bigger calm sea. Zero leaves the water indifferent to the sky.
fluorite.options.rt.waveWarp.tooltip: How far the world the waves travel through is bent. This is what removes the lattice: a sum of ten plane waves is quasi-periodic whatever you do to it, because the phase relationships between components are the same everywhere, and bending the domain makes them drift with position instead. Measured, it cuts the long-range repetition by more than ten times. It is not a cheat -- real water refracts over currents and bends its crests this way. Silently capped at a quarter of the warp scale: past that the bend folds over itself and creases the surface, which shows as seams and rings.
fluorite.options.rt.waveWarpScale.toolti: How far apart the bends are. Large is a slow lazy wander across the sea; small churns the wave trains up close.
fluorite.options.rt.waveFirst.tooltip: Diagnostic. Which of the ten wave components the field starts at. Set this and the last one to the same number to see a single component alone.
fluorite.options.rt.waveLast.tooltip: Diagnostic. Which component the field stops at. Walk it up from 1 and watch the sea accumulate -- the step where an artefact appears is the component responsible, which a sum of ten waves cannot otherwise tell you.
fluorite.options.rt.waveBandLimit.toolti: Fades short waves out as they get too small for the ray to resolve. Turning it OFF is wrong -- it aliases badly at distance -- and that is the point: it is here so a ring or a boundary line on the water can be attributed. If a line vanishes with this off, it was a component fading out at a fixed distance rather than anything in the waves themselves.
fluorite.options.rt.waterDeformMode.tool: Which water is BUILT ready to deform. 'all' removes the boundary entirely, so no section is ever rebuilt for crossing it and the rebuild flicker cannot happen; it does not cost more per frame, because the displacement still only touches water near you. What it costs is fixed memory, and BLAS compaction given up on water sections. 'near' is the low-memory option and keeps the flicker. BOTH THIS AND THE DEFORMATION SWITCH TAKE EFFECT ON THE NEXT WORLD LOAD -- whether a section can deform is decided when it is built, and nothing rebuilds a section because a setting changed. Turning deformation off still stops it immediately; turning it on needs the reload.
fluorite.options.rt.waveSpeed.tooltip: How fast the whole sea moves. Uniform on purpose: it scales every wave equally, so the relation between them survives and long swell still strides past while short chop flutters in place. There is deliberately no per-wavelength speed control, because that relation is the biggest single thing that reads as water. The weather does not act here -- in deep water a wave's speed depends only on its length, so a storm reaches the speed by making waves LONGER, which makes them faster on their own.
fluorite.options.rt.fogTimeGain.tooltip: How much thicker the fog gets around dawn. This is radiation fog, the kind that lies over a landscape in the early morning: the ground radiates its heat away overnight and the air above it cools until its water condenses, so the mist is thickest when the ground is coldest -- just before sunrise, not at midnight. The sun then burns it off through the morning, and the clearest air of the day is mid-afternoon. Zero leaves the fog the same at every hour.
fluorite.options.rt.fogWeatherGain.toolt: Fog-density gain at full rain. The response is continuous from clear to downpour; thunder has its own additional gain in Weather Effects.
Bake directional rain exposure and apply persistent wet-film and puddle responses to rain-exposed opaque surfaces.
Resolution of the map that decides what is out in the weather. Shared: it shelters snowflakes from a roof exactly as it shelters raindrops, and it is what keeps surfaces under cover dry.
fluorite.options.rt.rainSlantDegrees.too: How far precipitation leans from vertical, along the wind heading. Shared by rain and snow, and it is also the direction the shelter map traces, so it decides what counts as being under a roof.
fluorite.options.rt.wetFillSeconds.toolt: Seconds of full rain needed for the global wet film to fill from dry to saturated.
fluorite.options.rt.wetDrySeconds.toolti: Base seconds for a saturated wet film to dry. Daylight and cloud cover may slow this when Daylight Drying is enabled.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleFillSeconds.to: Seconds of full rain needed to fill the global puddle reservoir.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleDrySeconds.too: Base seconds for full puddle storage to evaporate after rain stops.
fluorite.options.rt.daylightDrying.toolt: Let daylight and cloud cover change evaporation. Noon approaches the authored drying time; night or heavy overcast falls toward one quarter speed.
fluorite.options.rt.wetFilmStrength.tool: Strength of the energy-layered water reflection over wet materials. The water IOR remains physically fixed at 1.333.
fluorite.options.rt.wetFilmRoughness.too: Linear GGX alpha of the rain film. Lower values make a sharper reflection; this also reaches the continuation sampler and RR guide.
fluorite.options.rt.puddlesEnabled.toolt: Add an independent smooth world-anchored standing-water field controlled by slope and material storage.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleCoverage.toolt: Largest fraction of suitable rain-exposed ground selected by the world-space puddle field at full storage.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleScale.tooltip: World-space size of broad puddle structures. The field is fixed to the world and never follows the camera.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleRippleStrength: Normal-map strength of the damped impact waves on puddles and native water. This changes reflected-light distortion, not ripple radius or event density.
fluorite.options.rt.rainRippleSize.toolt: Maximum radius of an analytic raindrop ring on puddles and native water, in blocks.
fluorite.options.rt.wetDarkeningGain.too: Temporary global multiplier over material wet darkening. This will be baked to a constant after visual calibration.
fluorite.options.rt.wetCoatGain.tooltip: Temporary multiplier over water-film coverage. It does not change the physical water IOR or F0.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleLayerGain.tool: Temporary multiplier over standing-water layer coverage after storage, material affinity and basin selection.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleRoughness.tool: Linear GGX alpha of the standing-water interface. Lower values make reflections sharper.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleExtraDarkening: Small additional substrate darkening beyond the shared wet-material endpoint. It is capped at 25%; Fresnel reflection already removes most of the substrate energy under shallow standing water.
fluorite.options.rt.puddleNormalFlatteni: How strongly standing water replaces the substrate normal with a level water interface.
fluorite.options.rt.wetFilmNormalFlatten: Temporary reduction of the original material's small-scale normal relief under a thin wet film. Standing puddles add their stronger flattening continuously on top.
fluorite.options.rt.rainRippleWidth.tool: Base width of impact rings before footprint-aware anti-aliasing.
fluorite.options.rt.defaultWetAbsorption: Fallback porosity for materials without a format-3 weather override; controls how quickly the visible wet response saturates.
Maximum albedo darkening for materials without an authored weather value.
fluorite.options.rt.defaultWetFilm.toolt: How strongly an unconfigured material retains a reflective surface film.
fluorite.options.rt.defaultPuddleAffinit: How readily an unconfigured material participates in standing-water patches.
fluorite.options.rt.rainParticlesEnabled: Draw falling precipitation -- rain streaks AND snowflakes, plus rain's splashes. One switch because they are one pass: what falls in a given column is decided by its biome, not by a setting.
fluorite.options.rt.rainStreakQuality.to: The upper bound on how many falling particles exist at once. Shared by rain and snow: whichever is falling draws from the same budget, so the cost is the same either way.
fluorite.options.rt.rainStreakDensity.to: How much of the budget a full downpour or snowfall actually uses. Shared by rain and snow -- turning it down thins both.
fluorite.options.rt.rainStreakSpeed.tool: World-space speed of procedural droplets. Exposure and impacts keep the same direction but do not depend on this artistic speed.
fluorite.options.rt.rainStreakLength.too: World-space length of each visible droplet streak.
fluorite.options.rt.snowFallSpeed.toolti: How fast snow falls. It cannot share rain's dial: rain defaults to 24 blocks a second against a snowflake's terminal velocity of about 1 to 1.5, so one slider moving both would be wrong for one of them. At the default a flake takes about twenty seconds to cross the fall span, which is why its drift comes from a shared turbulence field rather than a per-flake wobble.
fluorite.options.rt.snowFlakeSize.toolti: How wide a snowflake is drawn. Pure style: a real aggregate flake is two to ten millimetres, far below a pixel at any render distance, so every game draws them enormously oversized and this is how much. Never smaller than one pixel, so distant snow thins out instead of flickering.
fluorite.options.rt.rainSplashTarget.too: Target live RT splash pool around the camera. Splashes are selected from the same deterministic events as ripple rings; collision and visibility can make the exact on-screen count lower.
fluorite.options.rt.rainSplashSize.toolt: Temporary size of Fluorite's neutral procedural impact crowns and droplets.
fluorite.options.rt.rainSplashOpacity.to: Temporary stochastic coverage of procedural RT impact splashes.
fluorite.options.rt.rainSplashBrightness: Temporary brightness multiplier for the neutral pale-water tint. It changes reflected color but does not make the splash emissive.
fluorite.options.rt.fogThunderDensityGai: Additional fog-density gain at full thunder, on top of rain. Negative values can reduce fog; the final physical density is never allowed below zero.
fluorite.options.rt.fogTimeStructureGain: Signed change to 3D fog contrast at the peak of the radiation-fog day curve. Zero keeps the authored contrast unchanged.
fluorite.options.rt.fogRainStructureGain: Signed change to 3D fog contrast at full rain. Negative values make rain haze more uniform; positive values make it more broken up.
fluorite.options.rt.fogThunderStructureG: Additional signed change to 3D fog contrast at full thunder. The mean density remains controlled by the density settings.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudRainCoverageBia: Signed coverage-field bias at full rain. Positive fills clearings; negative opens them.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudRainDensityGain: Cloud-density gain at full rain. The final density is kept non-negative.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudThunderTypeBias: Signed cloud-type bias at full thunder. Positive grows the deck toward taller storm cells.
fluorite.options.rt.waterRainScatterGain: Suspended-particle scattering gain at full rain. Total extinction changes with it because water extinction is absorption plus scattering.
fluorite.options.rt.waterThunderScatterG: Additional suspended-particle scattering gain at full thunder. Zero leaves the clear-weather water coefficients unchanged.
How strongly weather shifts emphasis from the existing short wave bands toward the existing long bands. Wavelengths and phases never change, so crests do not jump; a unit weather transition is spread linearly over 20 seconds. 0 keeps the spectrum balance unchanged, 1 gives the largest transfer.
fluorite.options.rt.waterCausticStrength: Upper bound for underwater caustic contrast. Dense fog and cloud weather fade both bright folds and their compensating dark regions toward neutral together, rather than adding or removing mean sunlight. The current cloud response is a global weather approximation until the planned 2D cloud sun-transmittance map is available.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseEnabled.tool: Use the world-anchored 3D density field. Off exits before every field sample and numerical heterogeneous march, returning to the exact analytic-height fog; the pre-baked 8 MB texture remains allocated for instant A/B testing.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseContrast.too: One is the calibrated field. Higher values push clumps and clear pockets apart through a bounded mean-preserving curve: local density stays within 0..2 and its average stays one.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseFieldScale.t: World-space size of one repeating 3D field. Broad structures are one quarter of this size and detail one sixteenth.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseWindSpeed.to: How fast the density field drifts in blocks per second. It is independent of the cloud wind.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseWindOffset.t: How far the near-ground fog runs off the global wind direction. Its speed remains independent of both cloud layers.
fluorite.options.rt.fogNoiseMarchSteps.t: Maximum density samples in one contiguous numerical interval. More steps resolve structure farther along a ray but increase froxel, reflection and GI cost.
fluorite.options.rt.preset.export.toolti: Export every portable Fluorite setting to a versioned TOML preset. Machine-local paths and diagnostics are omitted.
fluorite.options.rt.preset.import.toolti: Strictly validate and replace the portable configuration. Safe settings apply now; resource settings wait for restart.
fluorite.options.rt.preset.import.succes:
Applied %s setting changes live.
%s setting changes are pending restart.
%s system-property overrides remain active.
Backup: %s
fluorite.options.rt.preset.error.title: Preset Operation Failed
fluorite.options.rt.resetDefaults.confir: This replaces every Fluorite setting and clears pending restart choices. This cannot be undone unless you exported a preset first.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudWarpAmount.tool: How far a cloud's shape is pushed around before it is drawn, in blocks. This displaces the cloud's surface rather than eating into it, which is the difference between clouds that billow and clouds that are round blobs with frayed edges. The warp drifts at its own speed, so shapes grow and dissolve as the sky moves instead of sliding past unchanged. Zero turns it off entirely.
fluorite.options.rt.cloudWarpScale.toolt: How large the billows are, in blocks. Large values reshape whole lobes of a cloud; small values fray its edges into wisps.
How fast a cloud's shape changes, separately from how fast it drifts. Clouds are reshaped by convection rather than by wind -- a cumulus on a still afternoon billows and dissolves without going anywhere -- so this does not follow the wind speed, and setting the wind to zero no longer freezes the sky. Higher makes lobes grow and dissolve faster; too high and the cloud boils instead of growing.
